mainTopic: Why animals from a fixed mixture may not be offered (רבא's גזירה), and whether one offered anyway still counts
overview: The גמרא asks why a forbidden animal mixed into a group of permitted קרבנות is not simply cancelled by the majority. The first answer is that the animals are קבוע (fixed in place), and anything fixed counts as a 50/50 doubt. The גמרא then suggests pushing the animals so they move, so that each one that wanders off follows the majority. רבא answers that חכמים made a גזירה against this. His first reason, that ten כהנים might offer them all at once, is challenged with the מגיסא. His second reason, that ten כהנים might take them at once, is rejected as unrealistic. His final reason is that the גזירה protects the rule of קבוע. רבא then rules that if someone offered one of these animals anyway, it does not count (לא מרצי). רב הונא בר יהודה challenges this from a משנה in קנים, where mixed bird offerings still partly count after the fact. The גמרא answers that the two sources follow opposite views on whether בעלי חיים נדחין. It then begins a new challenge: slaughtered offerings are נדחין according to everyone, and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The animals are fixed, so the majority rule does not work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects cancelling the forbidden animal by majority, because the animals are קבוע, and anything קבוע counts as half and half.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anything fixed is treated as if it were half and half!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues an argument from just before this text. It pushes back on the idea that the forbidden animal is cancelled by the majority, because the animals are standing fixed in their place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually a forbidden item in a majority of permitted items follows the majority. But when the items are קבוע, still sitting in their fixed spot, the rule changes: the doubt counts as an even 50/50, no matter how big the majority is. So the majority cannot help here.

keyTerms.meaning: Fixed: an item still sitting in its place within the group
As if half and half, an even 50/50 doubt
Is considered, is treated like

steps.confusionAlert: קבוע does not mean the majority is small. Even with a huge majority, a fixed item is treated as a 50/50 doubt.
steps.whyThisMatters: The whole rest of the sugya tries to get around this rule, so this is the key problem to keep in mind.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל קָבוּעַ כְּמֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה דָּמֵי!
phrases.english: And anything fixed is considered like half and half!
phrases.notes: This finishes an argument that started before this text: the animals are still standing together in one place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכׇל קָבוּעַ כְּמֶחֱצָה עַל מֶחֱצָה דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion about cancelling the forbidden animal by majority.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using majority to permit the mixed animals while they stand fixed.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A fixed mixture is treated as an even doubt, so majority does not apply.

steps.title: Suggestion: make the animals move so the majority rule applies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests pushing the animals so they move around and are no longer fixed. Then any animal that leaves the group can be treated as coming from the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let us push them so they move around, and then say: anything that separates, separates from the majority!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a way around the קבוע problem: make the animals move, so they are no longer fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule of קבוע only applies while the items sit in place. Once the animals are scattered, each one that walks off can follow the rule of כל דפריש מרובא פריש, so it counts as permitted. This puts pressure on the law that none of the animals may be offered: why not just do this?

keyTerms.meaning: Let us push them, press them along
So that they move around
Whatever separates is assumed to come from the majority

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a trick to change the facts. It uses a real halachic difference: an item that leaves a moving group follows the majority, but an item taken from a fixed group is a 50/50 doubt.

phrases.english: Rather, let us push them so that they move,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא, and the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean the animals move around.

phrases.english: and let us say: whatever separates, separates from the majority!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a way around the קבוע problem raised in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that none of the mixed animals may be offered.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If moving the animals removes the קבוע status, each animal that separates follows the majority and should be permitted.

steps.title: רבא: a גזירה in case ten כהנים offer them all at once
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that since חכמים said none may be offered, there must be a גזירה: maybe ten כהנים will come together and offer the animals all at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now that חכמים said we do not offer them, it must be a decree, in case ten כהנים come at the same time and offer them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the suggestion. Moving the animals might work in principle, but חכמים made a גזירה against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If many כהנים offer many animals at once, the forbidden one is surely among them, and the majority rule no longer protects anyone. To avoid that, חכמים forbade the whole method. So the ruling is a rabbinic safeguard, not a sign that the method fails by Torah law.

keyTerms.meaning: Now that חכמים have said
A rabbinic decree made as a safeguard
All at once, at the same time

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now that the Sages said we do not offer it,
it is a decree, in case ten priests come
at the same time and offer them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַשְׁתָּא דַּאֲמוּר רַבָּנַן לָא נִיקְרַב
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Moving the animals should let each one be offered by the majority rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: חכמים forbade it, worried that ten כהנים would offer all the animals at once.

steps.title: A scholar asks: would the מגיסא then become forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: One of the חכמים challenges רבא: if the worry is offering together, then the large basin where all the parts are put together would become forbidden!
steps.simpleTranslation: One of the חכמים said to רבא: If so, is the מגיסא forbidden?!
steps.whatsHappening: A scholar attacks רבא's reason by pointing to the basin where the parts of the קרבנות are collected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once each animal was taken separately and allowed, its parts are placed together in the מגיסא before going on the מזבח. If offering together is the problem, those already-allowed animals would suddenly become forbidden again in the basin, which makes no sense. So the worry about offering together cannot be the reason.

keyTerms.meaning: If so, then according to your logic
A large basin or bowl for the parts of the קרבנות
Is forbidden

phrases.english: One of the Sages said to Rava:
If so, is the basin forbidden?!
phrases.notes: He means: animals already allowed one at a time would become forbidden again once their parts sit together in the basin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ הָהוּא מֵרַבָּנַן לְרָבָא: אֶלָּא מֵעַתָּה
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that the worry is ten כהנים offering together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Animals already allowed separately are put together in the מגיסא anyway, so offering together cannot make them forbidden.

steps.title: רבא: the worry is ten כהנים taking them all at once
steps.stepSummary: רבא adjusts his answer: the worry is not offering together, but that ten כהנים will take the animals out of the group all at the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is because of the worry that ten כהנים might come at the same time and take them.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא changes the focus of the גזירה from the moment of offering to the moment of taking the animals from the group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The majority rule works for an animal that separates by itself. If most of the animals are taken at once, the forbidden one is almost surely among them, so the rule does not protect them. This answers the basin question, because by the time the parts reach the basin each animal was already allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of
And they will take

phrases.english: It is because perhaps ten priests will come
at the same time and take them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם שֶׁמָּא יָבֹאוּ עֲשָׂרָה כֹּהֲנִים בְּבַת אַחַת וְיִקְחוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מגיסא challenge of step 4 by changing the worry from offering to taking.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing the reason for the גזירה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה is about offering the animals together.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה is about taking the animals from the group together.

steps.title: The גמרא asks: could ten כהנים really take them all at once?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רבא's second reason: it is not realistic that ten כהנים would grab the scattered animals at exactly the same time.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it possible for ten כהנים to do it at the same time?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רבא's adjusted reason as unrealistic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The animals have been scattered, and it is hard to picture ten כהנים each catching one at the very same moment. חכמים do not make a גזירה for something so unlikely, so this reason also falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it possible?! (said as a challenge)

phrases.aramaic: בַּעֲשָׂרָה כֹּהֲנִים בְּבַת אַחַת מִי אֶפְשָׁר?!
phrases.english: With ten priests at the same time, is that possible?!

steps.triggerLanguage: בַּעֲשָׂרָה כֹּהֲנִים בְּבַת אַחַת מִי אֶפְשָׁר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's reason that ten כהנים might take the animals at once.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Such a case is practically impossible, so it is not a reason for a גזירה.

steps.title: רבא's final reason: a גזירה because of קבוע
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new reason: the גזירה is because of קבוע. If we allow taking from a moving group, people may come to allow taking from a fixed group too.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It is because of קבוע.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא drops the ten כהנים idea and gives his final reason for the גזירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Moving the animals really does work by the letter of the law. But חכמים worried that people would confuse the cases and take an animal straight from the fixed group, where it is a 50/50 doubt. So they forbade the moving method too, to protect the rule of קבוע.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, רבא said (a new answer replacing the old one)

steps.whatToRemember: The ban on offering the mixed animals is a rabbinic גזירה. Moving them would work in principle, but חכמים forbade it so people would not come to take animals from a fixed (קבוע) group, where the doubt counts as 50/50.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that חכמים sometimes forbid a method that is truly allowed, to keep people from mixing it up with a forbidden case that looks similar.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It is because of a fixed item.
phrases.notes: He means: a decree, so people won't come to take an animal straight from the fixed group.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reason of step 5 with a new reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The גזירה is about ten כהנים acting at once.
steps.terutzMaskana: The גזירה exists so people will not come to take animals from a fixed group.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Moving the animals is forbidden by a rabbinic גזירה because of קבוע.

steps.title: If one offered from the mixture anyway, it does not count
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that because the חכמים said not to offer any animal from the mixture, an animal that was offered anyway does not bring כפרה to its owner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Now that the Rabbis said we may not offer any of them, if someone did offer one, it does not effect acceptance.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא moves from the question of why we may not offer the animals to a new question: what happens after the fact if someone did offer one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now the discussion was about the starting rule: we may not offer. רבא now says that this rule is so strong that even after the fact the קרבן fails. The owner gets no ריצוי.

keyTerms.meaning: We do not offer (the starting rule, before the fact)
Effects acceptance; brings כפרה for the owner
Now that they said: building a new rule on top of an earlier one

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole rest of the sugya, which tests whether something forbidden to offer can still work after the fact.

phrases.english: Rava said:
Now that the Rabbis say we do not offer any of them,
if one did offer one, it does not effect acceptance.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean 'offered.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָמְרִי רַבָּנַן לָא נַקְרֵיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the גזירה explained in steps 3-7 and draws a new after-the-fact rule from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An animal from the mixture that was offered anyway does not count for the owner (לא מרצי).

steps.title: Challenge from mixed-up bird offerings in קנים
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בר יהודה quotes a משנה. When a bird חטאת and a bird עולה get mixed, the starting rule is that all must die. But if a כהן offered them on his own, half are kosher. So something forbidden to offer can still count after the fact.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בר יהודה objected to רבא from a משנה. If a bird חטאת got mixed with a bird עולה, or an עולה with a חטאת, even one in ten thousand, they must all die. When is this said? When the כהן asks what to do. But if the כהן did not ask and did them all on top, half are kosher and half are not. If he did them all on the bottom, half are kosher and half are not. If he did one on the bottom and one on top, both are not kosher, because I say the חטאת was done on top and the עולה on the bottom.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בר יהודה attacks רבא's rule by quoting a משנה where offerings that should not have been brought still count after the fact.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the fact, the mixed birds are forbidden: 'they must all die.' Yet a כהן who offered them anyway gets half of them counted as kosher. This shows that being forbidden to offer does not make the קרבן fail after the fact, which is the opposite of רבא's 'לא מרצי.'

keyTerms.meaning: Got mixed up
In ten thousand
A כהן who first asks the בית דין what to do
Above or below the red line on the מזבח. A bird עולה is done above it and a bird חטאת below it.

steps.confusionAlert: 'Half are kosher' does not mean the כהן was allowed to do this. He was not. The point is only that after the fact, the ones done in their proper place count.

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna bar Yehuda raised an objection to Rava:
A sin offering that got mixed with a burnt offering,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in קנים, so it is talking about bird offerings.

phrases.english: or a burnt offering that got mixed with a sin offering,
even if it is one in ten thousand,
they must all die.
In what case is this said?
With a priest who asks what to do;
but with a priest who does not ask,
if he did them all above,
phrases.notes: Above the red line around the middle of the מזבח, the proper place for a bird עולה.

phrases.english: half are fit and half are unfit.
If he did them all below,
half are fit and half are unfit.
If he did one below and one above,
both are unfit,
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected, feminine form. Both mean 'both of them.'

phrases.english: for I say:
the sin offering was offered above
and the burnt offering was offered below.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בַּר יְהוּדָה לְרָבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks רבא's after-the-fact rule from step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's ruling that an animal from a forbidden mixture, if offered, is לא מרצי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in קנים forbids offering the mixed birds before the fact, yet counts the properly done ones as kosher after the fact. So 'forbidden to offer' does not mean 'fails after the fact.'

steps.title: It depends on whether living animals become permanently pushed off
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבא and the משנה in קנים follow two opposite opinions. רבא follows the view that בעלי חיים נדחין, and קנים follows the view that בעלי חיים אינן נדחין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this ruling follows the one who says living animals are permanently pushed off, and that ruling follows the one who says living animals are not permanently pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא saves רבא by saying his rule and the משנה are each based on a different side of a known מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that once a live animal was disqualified by being in the mixture, it is pushed off forever, so offering it later does not help. The משנה in קנים holds that a live animal is not pushed off forever, so if it was offered properly it counts. רבא is not proven wrong; he simply follows the other opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: dropping the earlier assumption and giving a new answer
Following the one who says
Living animals that were disqualified are pushed off from the מזבח forever
Are not pushed off forever; they can become fit again

steps.whatToRemember: רבא's 'לא מרצי' rests on the view that בעלי חיים נדחין. The משנה in קנים follows the view that they are not נדחין, so the two do not contradict each other.
steps.confusionAlert: The answer does not say the משנה in קנים is wrong. It says the two sources follow two different תנאים.

phrases.english: Rather,

phrases.aramaic: הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִדְחִין,
phrases.english: this follows the one who says living animals are rejected,

phrases.aramaic: הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים אֵינָן נִידְחִין.
phrases.english: that follows the one who says living animals are not rejected.
phrases.notes: 'That' is the משנה in קנים quoted in step 9.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא הָא כְּמַאן דְּאָמַר בַּעֲלֵי חַיִּים נִדְחִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 by placing the two sources on opposite sides of a מחלוקת.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources between two opinions (תנאי היא).
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everyone agrees that an animal forbidden to offer still counts after the fact, as the משנה in קנים shows.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is a מחלוקת. Whoever holds בעלי חיים נדחין agrees with רבא that it does not count, and whoever holds אינן נדחין agrees with the משנה in קנים.

steps.title: Killed offerings are pushed off according to everyone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 10. That answer said the משנה in קנים follows the view that live animals are not pushed off. But killed offerings are pushed off according to everyone.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there are killed offerings, which everyone agrees are pushed off.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer it just gave in Step 10. It points out a case that the 'live animals are not pushed off' view does not cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מחלוקת about דחוי that step 10 relied on only applies to animals that are still alive. Once an offering has been slaughtered, both sides agree it can be pushed off for good. So for slaughtered offerings, the split between two opinions in step 10 does not work. The גמרא is setting up a source about slaughtered offerings, which comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: But there is; this word points to a case that causes a problem
Offerings that were already killed, as opposed to animals that are still alive
According to everyone; all opinions agree
They are pushed off, meaning they become permanently unfit to offer

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the מחלוקת from Step 10 covers every case. It is only about live animals. For offerings that were already killed, everyone agrees they can be pushed off.

phrases.english: But there are killed offerings
which according to everyone are pushed off

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of Step 10, which explained the משנה in קנים through the view that בעלי חיים אינן נדחין.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of step 10, which made רבא's ruling and the משנה in קנים depend on the מחלוקת about whether live animals are pushed off
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The split in step 10 only works for live animals. For slaughtered offerings, everyone agrees they are pushed off, so a case involving slaughtered offerings cannot be explained by assigning it to the view that they are not pushed off.
